kept.excerpt: Mohamed Salah is to bring the curtain down on his illustrious career with Liverpool FC at the end of the 2025-26 season. The forward has reached an agreement with the Reds that will see him close a remarkable nine-year chapter at Anfield.
kept.relevance: The official departure announcement establishes that Salah is leaving Liverpool, making his next club the relevant unresolved event.

kept.excerpt: Now without a club to his name, attention turns to where the 34-year-old will continue his career. Salah’s agent Ramy Abbas Issa released an update on Friday morning stating: “We still do not know where Mohamed will play next season but we may know very soon.” He added: “It is not our style to have discussions with clubs that Mohamed wouldn’t want to play for, just for the sake of noise.”
kept.relevance: The league’s dated report of the agent’s statement establishes free-agent status and uncertainty about the next destination.

kept.excerpt: TEAMtalk revealed in an update yesterday that Inter Miami, San Diego FC, and Sporting Kansas City from MLS have all been trying to convince Salah to join. Salah’s agent, Ramy Abbas Issa, posted on X earlier today: “We still do not know where Mohamed will play next season but we may know very soon.”
kept.relevance: Reported approaches from three MLS clubs identify competing destinations outside Süper Lig, although they do not establish any completed agreement.

kept.excerpt: Following reports that Mohamed Salah had agreed to sign for Turkish club Besiktas on a one-year contract, his agent, Ramy Abbas, immediately denied it and said no deal was in place with any club. Roughly two hours after the reports surfaced on social media, Abbas posted on X: “I personally do not know where Mohamed will play next season. What does that tell you?”
kept.relevance: The agent’s explicit denial prevents treating contemporaneous reports of a Beşiktaş agreement as an official signing.

kept.excerpt: According to information provided by our reporter Tayfun Akkaya, Beşiktaş president Serdal Adalı and Salah’s agent will hold a meeting on Thursday, July 23.
kept.relevance: The scheduled meeting provides recent evidence of active negotiations with a Süper Lig club immediately before the experiment cutoff.

kept.excerpt: No official agreement has yet been reached between Beşiktaş and Mohamed Salah. Adalı said: “Nothing has been completed regarding the Salah transfer yet.” He said the agents had raised their financial demands after reports that the transfer was finished, that the club had rejected those demands, and that negotiations were continuing. He added: “We love Salah very much and agree with the player on every issue, but everyone should know that our priority is Beşiktaş’s interests.”
kept.relevance: The cutoff-day report describes an unresolved financial obstacle despite claimed agreement with the player, supporting a distinction between ongoing Süper Lig negotiations and an official transfer.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: 2026-07-23, inclusive. Each included item has an explicit publication date in web-search evidence; no post-cutoff developments, outcome information, betting pages, odds, or market prices are included. Excerpts are source quotations or faithful factual condensations; Turkish excerpts are translated into English. The Dünya article was published July 23 at 15:24 and updated at 15:27; its presidential remarks repeat comments already reported on July 18 and should not be interpreted as a newly issued July 23 statement. The beIN article was published July 22 and updated the same day. Full-page verification was limited: web_fetch failed because of provider configuration, and the requested agent-reach fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so the pack relies on dated indexed source text returned by targeted web_search queries. Reported approaches and negotiations remain attributed claims; none of the included evidence establishes an official next-club signing.
